issue_context.body:

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Basically I have setup ZM and HA in docker and they work 100%, except after a reboot, HA fails to load ZM. I then restart HA and it works as expected. Other entities that don't work on boot, generally just "fix themselves" over a bit of time as the services all become available. HA should do the same with the ZM integrations.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 
```
bash-5.0# hass --version
0.108.4
```
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): 
`docker run --init -d --name="home-assistant" -e "TZ=America/Whitehorse" -v /opt/homeassistant/:/config --net=host homeassistant/home-assistant:stable`
- Integration causing this issue: 
`ZoneMinder`
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zoneminder/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```
#ZoneMinder
zoneminder:
  - host: domain.tld
    ssl: true
    verify_ssl: false
    username: uname
    password: pwd

camera:
  - platform: zoneminder

sensor:
  - platform: zoneminder
    include_archived: false

switch:
  - platform: zoneminder
    command_on: Modect
    command_off: Monitor
```

```

<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```

```txt

```

## Additional information

I start both HA and ZM via SystemD in Docker Containers at boot. I figure ZM isn't started/running when HA starts and it's understandable the entity/sensors etc don't work straight away, but I would exepect them to sort themselves out in a few minutes as ZM becomes responsive. It seems that HA just "gives up" after having errors during starting/setting up component. Can this be resolved somehow without me hacking delays into systemd/cron/scripts etc?

Thanks and loving HA so far!!
comments: Hey there @rohankapoorcom, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`zoneminder`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L459) for? Thanks!

This is a little complicated because of the mechanism that allows integrations to retry their setups (as far as I remember), is based on config entries. Zoneminder doesn't use config entries yet because the api doesn't expose a unique ID field needed for the entry registry.

Unless there is a way around that, I'm not sure it's possible to retry config without restarting Home Assistant. 

Do you have a dependency on zoneminder set in systemd for home assistant? That may be an easier solution.

@rohankapoorcom  I have a question on how to do that posted on UandL SE https://unix.stackexchange.com/q/581929/130767 but I thought I would make a post here as well to see if it could be resolved at the root of the problem so to speak. If you could answer my question on how to make my homeassistant systemd script dependant on zoneminder being booted first I could try that. I worried that it will still need a hack for a delay as zoneminder takes a bit to boot up but I'd be willing to try!

I'm not sure it systemd can do it, but I've done things like this before using docker compose: https://8thlight.com/blog/dariusz-pasciak/2016/10/17/docker-compose-wait-for-dependencies.html

I don't love the two services being coupled though.

I tried messing with systemd, but found this to be a better "hack", as it should resolve this issue with anything else in the future.

```
cat << 'EOF' >/etc/cron.d/ha_restart
@reboot root /opt/homeasssitant/harestart.sh
EOF
chmod +x /etc/cron.d/ha_restart
```
```
cat << 'EOF' >/opt/homeasssitant/harestart.sh
#!/bin/bash

sleep 30
systemctl restart home-assistant

touch /tmp/harestart #Just to confirm it ran
EOF
chmod +x /opt/homeasssitant/harestart.sh
```
I submitted a pull request that implements config flows and the reconnect on boot logic. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/37060

review_comments: We don't support mixing platform config and config entries. That should just be a migration. The platform config sections should be deprecated. What's the plan for the future?
`hass.async_add_job` is legacy for general use. If we need to schedule a job on the executor thread pool use `hass.async_add_executor_job`.
We normally patch the integration `async_setup_entry` to avoid setting up the whole integration on create entry results.
Our standard is to label both the deprecation PR and the invalidation PR as breaking.
Don't call config entry methods directly, except the mock `add_to_hass`. Use `hass.config_entries.async_unload`.
Why do we call this?
We don't need to start the config flow. Just set up the config entry is enough. Add a MockConfigEntry with the correct config as data parameter.
Please don't assert integration details. Only assert core state. That's the state machine, the service registry, the entity registry, the device registry or the config entry.
Isn't this a breaking change because the name is now changing?
No. The unique_id of the config is the host name. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/37060/files#diff-50e12b59b701cc09cf1dd70145ff9dcbR96
We still need this method call to filter out a bunch of useless urllib3 logging that spams the Home Asssistant log otherwise.
The filter setting should be moved to `async_setup_entry`.
Why is this necessary? Couldn't the user not want the cameras, sensors, switches, etc., but still want to use the service?
It's here for cleanup. If this is the last config to be removed, then remove the service too.
I changed the comment to be a bit more clear about why this is happening.
Ah yes, this makes much more sense now! Thanks for tweaking the comment.

Prefacing this with the fact that I'm not an expert on config flows / config entries.... so apologies if this is an obvious question. Once this data is stored in the config entry how does the user make changes to it?
For that matter how does a user set this from the config UI when they are first setting up from the config UI (if they didn't have the configuration.yaml imported in?)

Currently, HASS has no ability to change the initial options of a config entry. This is a forthcoming feature to HASS however.
For the switch platform, the user will have to configure this from yaml just like they did before. Upon HASS startup or creation of a new entry (via import or from UI), HASS will run the config entry through this platform's setup function.

I've just finished a full read of all of the code in the PR and wanted to double check one other thing:

Since the unique_ id is generated from the hostname/monitorid and the on/off state names of the created switch, when the user makes a change to an on/off value in the yaml configuration, this will create a new switch entity (without removing the old one) because the unique_id will have changed (since we don't have the way for UI editing yet).

The user would then be able to simply delete the old entity via the UI right?
Why are we testing the availability twice in the user flow?
We can use asyncio.gather here.
We prefer to import individual constant names instead of modules.
Is it worth making the zm_client a shared fixture used with all of the tests?
I don't think so. Each test sets up the client in unique ways. Abstracting it out to a fixture would only save ~2 lines per test. I don't think this savings is worth he extra test complexity.
